# dsh-model-garden
A **model picker for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI** (`dsh web`) that replaces the native composer mod
el seat with a table-style picker: searchable, sortable, filterable down to model capabilities, with
prices, live per-task cost, a rich detail card and a pinned default model for every sub-agent.
## Why
The stock selector lists models. Model Garden answers the questions you actually have while picking
one: *what does it cost right now, which routes are cheap enough, which models can see images, which
can call tools, which are deprecated, and which model should every sub-agent use* — and it keeps th
ose answers in sync with your providers.
## Features
### Picker and list
- **Table-style list** grouped by provider — click `Name`, `Ctx` or `Price` to sort (asc → desc → ba

ck to grouped), collapsible groups, per-provider counts
- **Keyboard-first** — `↑ ↓` navigate, `Home

`/`End` jump, `Enter` select, `Esc` close
- **Instant search** across names, ids, descriptions and p
rovider names — **and the model's facts**: `vision`, `tool calling`, `reasoning`, `structured output
`, `attachments`, `open weights`, `temperature`, `interleaved`, family, knowledge cutoff, release da

te and `deprecated`
- **Favorites** (⭐, persisted) and a **hidden models/providers blacklist** (✕ on

hover, managed in the ⚙ panel, persisted) — the blacklist never touches your DSH configuration
- **
Local / Live awareness** — providers are flagged *local* by their real endpoint (loopback / RFC1918
/ LAN hostnames, never by price), and local gateways are probed for the models they currently serve
### Advanced search (facet sheet)
The **Filters** button opens a two-column sheet above the picker. Every option carries the number of
models it would match, and the header counts the result (`Filters · 12 of 88`):
| Group | Options |

| **Scope** | Local only · Live only · Favorites only |
| **Capabilities** | Tool calling · Vision ·
Reasoning · Effort levels · Open weights · Structured output · Attachments · Temperature · Interlea

ved |
| **Limits** | Context ≥ 32K…1M · Input price ≤ $0.50/$1/$3/$10 · Knowledge cutoff year · Fami

ly |
| **Lifecycle** | Deprecated only |
| **Providers** | one provider from a dropdown (Configured
/ Hidden, each with its model count) |
Everything is derived from **your** installation at runtime — no provider, model or family name is h
is derived from **your** installation at runtime — no provider, model or family name is hard-coded:

- providers, counts and the `hidden` flag come from the live directory and your blacklist
- capabili
ty counts, families, knowledge years, context sizes and prices come from the models.dev catalog cach

e
- an option with **zero matches is disabled**, and a whole group is **not rendered** when your cat

alog cannot fill it (a local-only setup still gets Scope, Lifecycle and Providers)
- the Context lad
der only offers thresholds your models can reach; the knowledge years are the ones in your catalog
Filters combine with the text search (AND). **Reset** is always visible (dimmed while nothing is set
), clears every filter and leaves the search text alone.
### Detail card
Hovering a row opens the detail card as a **fixed companion to the picker**: left gutter, 1 px seam,
shared bottom edge. On narrow windows it moves **above** the picker instead of hanging off screen,
and it is height-clamped to the viewport.
The card is a **table** (`Property | Value`) with sections:
- **Model** — context, max output, reasoning efforts, price per 1M (in / out / cache read / cache wr

ite)
- **Capabilities** — modalities, tool calling, structured output, temperature, attachments, ope

n weights, interleaved reasoning
- **Lifecycle** — knowledge cutoff, release date, last update, depr

ecation status, family, aliases, canonical id
- **Provider** — route, models.dev provider and env ke
y, local-gateway metadata, provenance of each source
Facts merge three sources (DSH adapter via `llm.resolveModelInfo`, models.dev, and the raw `/models`
record of a local gateway) and are cached, so the first hover after a restart is never blank.
## How it works
The package is a **static profile plugin** with two halves:
| Half | File | Role |
| Client | `client.js` | Registers the `conversation.input.model` slot (shadowing the native seat) a

nd renders the picker, filter sheet, detail card and effort dropdown |
| Host | `index.js` | Same-or
igin JSON routes on the harness `webServer`, catalog/detail caches, and the sub-agent enforcement on

`agents.create` / `agents.resume` |
| Shared logic | `lib/refresh-core.js`, `lib/pi-catalog.js`, `l
ib/detail-core.js`, `lib/subagent-core.js` | Dependency-free, unit-tested pieces: provider discovery
+ merge, pi-ai catalog loading, detail-card merge rules, sub-agent override semantics |
## Compatibility
- Developed and tested against **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1** (rc.4 and rc.5) and carries the 0.1 code p
aths: provider routes are read through `ctx.configEditor` on 0.2 and through the legacy settings doc
ument on 0.1; writes go through the profile's configuration editor (0.2) with the old deep-merge as

fallback
- The client half is plain React through `window.__ModuleLoader__`; no build step, no depen

dencies
- The sub-agent override rides on `meta.origin: "subagent"` / `parentAgent` — the same seam

`dsh-subagent` uses
- The cost endpoints read the durable session log through the session facade (`s

napshotEvents()`, falling back to `ownEvents()` / `events`)
- Capability, price, family and knowledg
e filters need the models.dev catalog; without it the sheet simply offers the subset your data can f
ilters need the models.dev catalog; without it the sheet simply offers the subset your data can fill
> Slot note: the client declares `remote` + `remote.session` in its inject list. `modelDirectories.d
irectoryFor()` reaches into `ctx.remote.session`, and a cordis proxy binds `ctx` to the calling fibe
r — without those declarations the slot's inject factory throws and the native picker takes the seat
thout those declarations the slot's inject factory throws and the native picker takes the seat back.
